friction.description: Default `python` is 3.11.15 and tools/los.py refuses it; the fresh world has no .venv. The ImportError names two fixes (make setup, or an outside-repo uv venv) so recovery was mechanical, but no read works before setup.

CLAUDE.md hard rule 6 / §7 route 'what next' through a freshly rebuilt coordination view and generated/domain-atlas.md; OPERATOR.md routes it through bootstrap --brief + inspect coordination and says interfaces must not read generated prose. A first-time agent has to pick one.

Resume pointer is labelled 'confirmed' while the study map's current_stage names an earlier stage (and marks the pointer's stage 'pending'); the discrepancy is only visible by comparing two fields of the brief and inspecting the maps. No command reports it.

bootstrap --brief is a single-line JSON blob with no as-of date or days-until and mixes past (July) and future deadlines; resume gives day counts but only for the pointer's module. Computing 'due soon' needed manual date arithmetic across two outputs.

reads_before_first_answer_in_order: ls -a / git log of the world repository
uv venv + uv pip install (outside repo, per error hint)
unsure_about_and_resolution: Which doc governs 'what next' (CLAUDE.md vs OPERATOR.md) -> followed OPERATOR.md, the declared entry point.
Today's date -> used the machine clock (2026-09-24), which is also what `resume` uses for its day counts.
Which stage is current -> not resolved by the product; surfaced to the learner as a disagreement between the resume pointer / workspace notes and the study maps.
Whether to run `make setup` (writes into the repo) -> chose the error hint's outside-the-repository venv to keep orientation read-only.

uncertainties: Whether the resume-pointer vs study-map stage disagreement is intended world state (learner never updated stage progress) or a projection issue; not investigated further to avoid reading implementation.
Whether a real first-time agent would have the CLAUDE.md contract in context: here it was auto-loaded because the host repository carries an identical copy.
